ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners, as amended; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies, as amended; CSSF Regulation 12-02 and CSSF Circular 18/698; FATF Recommendations incorporated through EU AML/CFT Directives; and the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention as applied in Luxembourg.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of legal existence / good standing of each corporate limited partner or shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of commerce and companies in the country of origin of each corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; for non-Hague countries, Consular Legalization by a Luxembourg embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and current residential proof of each natural-person beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority of the beneficial owner's country of residence / municipality issuing proof of address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature certification plus Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-wealth/source-of-funds file of ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship bank or financial institution holding the UBO account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original banker's letter with Apostille or Consular Legalization if bank signature authentication is required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney / board resolution appointing the Luxembourg domiciliation and filing agent for the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or equivalent corporate governance body of the appointing shareholder or limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Screening of all UBOs, general partners, senior managers and authorized signatories against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN List and Luxembourg national sanctions; mandatory PEP identification under FATF Recommendation 12 with enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, and heightened monitoring for foreign PEPs, their family members and close associates. The AML/KYC file must document the screening platform used, timestamp and false-match resolution. Additional risk indicators are required for cross-border herbal botanical transactions invoiced from non-EU jurisdictions and for payment rails using Swift_TT or Wire_Transfer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory filings and official contracts are principally in French; a company or partnership name must be submitted in Latin letters and may be in French, German, English or another language provided a French transliteration or translation is filed. The legal form shall be stated as 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp', which may be preceded or followed by the chosen name. Non-Latin script names are refused until a certified transliteration is lodged.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Luxembourg does not operate a statutory name-reservation file; the name is checked online through the LBR and, if available, is retained only until filing is completed. If the RCS rejects a name, a written motivated refusal is issued; the applicant may within 30 days submit an e-mail or preregistered letter to the RCS requesting an administrative review, attaching the refusal notice and a proposed distinguishing element. If the refusal concerns a prohibited or sensitive token, the promoter must first obtain prior ministerial authorization from the Ministry of the Economy. A further appeal lies to the Tribunal administratif within three months of the final administrative refusal, in accordance with the Law of 7 November 1996 organizing administrative procedure.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible in principle through a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent, which must provide a physical registered office and accept mail. A purely virtual 'mailbox only' address is not bankable and does not satisfy the RCS location rule for partnerships. For an ISIC 4631 wholesale SCSp, the registered office should be accompanied by local manager or supervisor functions, contract records, bank account management and accounting substance in Luxembourg.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low only for a compliant SCSp: approximately 5-10% probability within the first 12 months, primarily through random RCS integrity checks and indirect evaluation by banks or AML officers. The probability rises to 20-30% where the partnership is flagged for low effective substance, high-risk counterparties, or repeated amendments to the UBO register.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg Business Registers name clearance, search certificates and preliminary feasibility analysis

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory LBR search fee schedule (EUR 20-EUR 50 per search) plus service provider search at EUR 90 per hour

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff under the Law of 9 December 1976 on notary tariffs; market benchmark for a standard SCSp deed is EUR 1,200-EUR 2,000 plus translation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS electronic filing, publication in the Recueil Electronique des Sociétés et Associations and issuance of RCS registration extract
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RCS e-filing fee schedule and RESA publication tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial UBO register filing in the Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory no-fee for initial beneficial-owner filing under the Law of 13 January 2019

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization bundle for origin-country KYC and corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs / Apostille authorities in each origin country; Luxembourg consulates for non-Hague countries

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark EUR 700-EUR 950 per year; no public statutory tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC pre-incorporation file, PEP/OFAC/UN sanctions screening and source-of-funds analysis
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm / AML compliance provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark EUR 250-EUR 400 per hour; fixed fee for a standard low-risk SCSp

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Tax registration applications (VAT / RCET), national identification number registration and administrative expediting
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA; Luxembourg Business Registers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory registration fee for VAT/RCET; third-party expediting costs, if any, at market rate

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, particularly Article 101-103 (Société en Commandite Spéciale) as introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 January 2014 on the RCS
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Association (Statuts / Contrat de société) filed electronically through the Luxembourg Business Registers portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital; no escrow account requirement. The capital is freely determined in the partnership agreement and may be credited in cash or in kind.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the formation of [Company Name], an SCSp organised under Luxembourg law, be and is hereby ratified; the draft articles of association as presented are approved in final form; the registered office is fixed at [Address], Luxembourg; the initial partnership interests are subscribed by the limited partner at a total capital as stated in the contribution schedule; and the undersigned manager/[General Partner] is authorised to execute all formation filings, open bank accounts, and take all aspects to obtain registrations, licences, and administrative permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and authentication of articles of association and partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (optional unless real estate contribution) or corporate counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and review the articles of association, partnership agreement, and ancillary governance documents. Ensure full compliance with the Law of 10 August 1915 and the SCSp rules. Execute the deed by all partners; notarise only if contributions include real estate or if the parties so choose. Prepare the declaration of conformity if required.
required_dossiers: Draft declaration of conformity (if submitted by a lawyer/service provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revise and re-execute the deed promptly; no formal appeal is needed at this pre-filing stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS online filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed articles of association, declaration of conformity, proof of registered office address, and identification documents for the general partner and manager through the LBR portal. Pay the applicable e-filing fee online. Receive the RCS registration number and corporate identity details.
required_dossiers: Signed articles of association (including notarial deed if notarised)
Declaration of conformity and legalisation by a professional admitted before the RCS
Proof of registered office address (lease or consortium agreement)
Identity card / passport and residence permit of the general partner and appointed manager
Power of attorney if filing through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend the filing in the LBR portal after receiving the query; resubmit the corrected package; if the filing is definitively rejected, file an appeal before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within one month of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the RESA electronic compendium
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the RCS registration is completed, the LBR automatically transmits the extract to the RESA for publication. Verify the published data within 5 working days; request correction if any discrepancy exists.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notify LBR of any inaccuracy; LBR publishes a corrective statement. If publication is delayed, contact LBR directly to expedite.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the commercial establishment authorisation (business licence)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for SMEs (Direction générale PME) via Guichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an application for an establishment authorisation under the Law of 2 September 2011 on business licensing. Provide the required professional qualifications, criminal record extracts, and business plan. Submit the application online or by post, pay the administrative fee, and obtain the autorisation d'établissement.
required_dossiers: Criminal record extract (bulletin n°3) for the manager and general partner
Proof of professional qualification or experience relevant to wholesale food trade
Lease or ownership proof of the business premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the file is incomplete, supply the requested documents to the ministry; if refused, a written appeal to the Minister of the Economy may be lodged within one month of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, social security and statistical registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Statec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online tax and social registrations through Guichet.lu within 15 days of the RCS registration. Apply for a Luxembourg VAT number, register with the CCSS if the company intends to employ staff, and obtain the Statec business number.
required_dossiers: ID or passport of the manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any incomplete information via Guichet.lu; the authorities usually allow a 15-day cure period. If VAT registration is delayed, follow up with the AEDT and provide a written explanation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Administration Luxembourgeoise Vétérinaire et Alimentaire (ALVA) – Unit for Foodstuffs, in coordination with the Ministry of Health (Direction de la Santé)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Sanitary Authorisation for the Wholesale Storage and Distribution of Dry Botanical Foodstuffs (Dried Goji Berries and Herbal Botanicals)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Environmental Protection Agency) – Luxembourg
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA – Category 10(a) of Annex II of the Law of 15 May 2018 (storage of non-perishable dry goods); simple administrative notification required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial effluent; sanitary wastewater discharges to municipal sewer in compliance with EU Urban Wastewater Directive 91/271/EEC; solid waste handling per EU Waste Framework Directive 2008/98/EC (waste code 20 03 01); no significant VOC emissions as no chemical processing is performed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Corps grand-ducal Incendie et Secours (CGDIS); building occupancy permit and structural load certificate from the Municipal Building Inspectorate; occupational health and safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (Administration des Contributions Directes, ACD) for income/corporate/wealth taxes; Luxembourg Indirect Tax and Registration Administration (Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA, AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration (Administration des Douanes et Accises) for export clearance. Integrated national e-portals: MyGuichet.lu and guichet.lu (business e-filing), Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) for entity registration, and the AEDT electronic VAT filing channel.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Notarial incorporation of the SCSp and filing with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS); the registration automatically generates the national identification number (matricule) which serves as the corporate tax reference. Step 2 — Within 15 days of commencing activity, file the VAT start-of-activity declaration (Form 640, declaration d'assujettissement à la TVA) with the AEDT via MyGuichet.lu; the AEDT issues a VAT identification number in the format 'LU' + 8 digits. Step 3 — A foreign non-resident entity making taxable supplies in Luxembourg without a local establishment must register directly with the AEDT (no de minimis threshold; a Luxembourg VAT representative may be required) and must provide proof of foreign establishment, articles of association, and bank references. Step 4 — The ACD opens the corporate income tax and municipal business tax files automatically upon RCS registration; annual returns are filed electronically via the eCDF module of MyGuichet.lu. Standard VAT registration processing time: 2–4 weeks.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — The SCSp is by default fiscally transparent under Luxembourg tax law: it is outside the scope of corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax (MBT), and net wealth tax (NWT); each partner is taxed on its distributive share of income as if realized directly (subject to the partner's residence and treaty position). For VAT, the SCSp has legal personality but is generally treated as a 'non-taxable person' for Luxembourg VAT purposes, with the partners jointly and severally regarded as the taxable persons carrying out the economic activity; however, where the partnership invoices in its own name, the SCSp may be registered for VAT as the invoicing vehicle. Territorial scope: transparency is a domestic-law default only; foreign characterization of the SCSp follows the relevant double tax treaty or foreign check-the-box rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: 1) Entity-level taxation option: the SCSp may elect under the law of 23 December 2016 to be treated as a Luxembourg tax-resident entity subject to CIT, MBT, and NWT ('opting partnership'), thereby also accessing the Luxembourg participation exemption; the election must be expressly provided in the partnership agreement and notified to the ACD, and it is irrevocable. 2) Hybrid-mismatch alignment: Luxembourg applies the ATAD hybrid mismatch rules (2018) and ATAD-2 branch/transparency rules (2020); partners may file alignment statements with the ACD to prevent double non-taxation or to allocate income consistently. 3) No U.S.-style check-the-box: the ACD does not provide an entity-classification form; the classification is evidenced through the partnership agreement, the RCS filing, and the election under (1).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée), administered under the Luxembourg VAT Law (Loi TVA) aligned with the EU VAT Directive (2006/112/EC).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 — no general turnover threshold for the SCSp: registration is mandatory for every economic operator established in Luxembourg from the date of RCS incorporation. A non-established foreign entity is likewise required to register for any taxable supply in Luxembourg unless the reverse-charge mechanism or the OSS/IOSS special schemes apply (EU cross-border distance-sales threshold: EUR 100,000). The optional small-business exemption (Art. 57 Loi TVA, annual turnover below EUR 35,000) is not available for export wholesale trading and does not eliminate the registration duty of an SCSp acting in its own name.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time transaction clearance, fiscal-data API, or digital stamping regime applies to B2B or export invoices in Luxembourg. Electronically issued invoices are valid without prior AEDT approval. A structured e-invoicing obligation (PEPPOL format) applies to B2G supplies to the Luxembourg central administration from 1 January 2024, extended to the broader public sector from 2025. For export transactions, the AEDT requires the full VAT-invoice content set under Art. 5 Loi TVA and compliant electronic retention of source documents for 10 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export VAT at 0% applies under Art. 42(I)(1) Loi TVA where the goods (i) are sold to a customer outside the EU, (ii) are physically dispatched or transported out of the EU customs territory, and (iii) are evidenced by export documentation issued in the supplier's name or by equivalent transport evidence accepted by AEDT practice. Dried goji berries (HS 1211/0813) and herbal botanicals must be accompanied, where the destination market requires it, by a phytosanitary certificate; zero-rating is independent of customs tariff status but is denied if the SAD/ECS export declaration contradicts the invoice (destination, recipient, INCOTERM). Export-related services (international transport, loading, handling) are zero-rated; services rendered to non-EU business customers fall outside Luxembourg VAT under the B2B place-of-supply rule where no Luxembourg nexus exists.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — SAD/summary declaration accepted through Luxembourg's ECS/ICS2 system (or the exporting EU Member State's customs office) evidencing the physical export
Bill of Lading (ocean), CMR waybill (road), or Air Waybill (air) in the name of the supplier/consignor showing the goods left the EU customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit proof (e.g., SWIFT MT103, account statement) evidencing the foreign customer's payment
Commercial invoice and pro-forma invoice cross-referencing the invoice number, HS classification 1211/0813, and the export declaration reference
Packing list, phytosanitary certificate, and EUR.1/certificate of origin (where the destination country applies preferential tariff treatment)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg law does not fix a statutory FX repatriation deadline for export VAT or CIT; the 180-day parameter is the prudent international trade benchmark used to evidence a genuine sale and to avoid transfer-pricing deemed interest adjustments on outstanding receivables. The AEDT audits export zero-rating claims on a documentary basis, with dried botanicals being a watch-listed category. Absence, inconsistency, or late production of the export-evidence package triggers retroactive reassessment of VAT at 17%, plus: (i) late-payment interest of 0.5% per month of outstanding tax; (ii) a civil delinquency surcharge of 5% per commenced month up to a maximum of 50% of the tax due; (iii) fixed administrative fines of EUR 250 to EUR 12,500 for formal record-keeping offenses; and (iv) for intentional fraud — including false SAD declarations, fabricated bills of lading, or round-tripping through shell customers — criminal prosecution under the 2018 tax-fraud reform with fines up to EUR 250,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years, plus joint and several liability of the SCSp's general partner for the evaded VAT and penalties. All export records must be retained for 10 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) — Central Bank of Luxembourg, operating within the Eurosystem; foreign-exchange and capital-control administration is liberalised under Article 63 TFEU, with prudential supervision shared by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible; Luxembourg imposes no exchange controls on current or capital account transactions. Inbound equity contributions, outbound trade settlements, and profit remittances from a fiscally transparent SCSp are unrestricted. Remittance frictions are confined to standard AML/KYC screening, EU/OFAC/UN sanctions compliance, CRS/FATCA UBO reporting, and documentary proof of the partnership's tax-transparent status (no Luxembourg withholding on distributions to non-resident partners).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies. Export receipts may be retained in the original currency (e.g., USD, CNY, EUR) or converted at the SCSp's commercial discretion. The only regulatory overlay is statistical: Luxembourg credit institutions report cross-border payments and external positions to the BCL for Eurosystem balance-of-payments statistics; the SCSp must preserve SWIFT MT103 records, commercial invoices, and bills of lading for audit and reconciliation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR multi-currency, SWIFT/SEPA); optional Capital Escrow Account for partner-committed funds
Operational Treasury Account (EUR/USD); dedicated trade-finance and documentary-credit desk

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate Operational Account with full EU/SEPA and correspondent-bank clearing
Operational Account plus FX/derivatives and structured trade-finance products
Multi-currency Cash Management and Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: MEDIUM as a supplementary collection/disbursement layer; LOW as the sole treasury anchor. Offshore digital EMIs (UK, Singapore, Hong Kong) lack PSD2 passporting rights into Luxembourg and cannot provide credit, overdrafts, or FX derivatives; EU/EEA-licensed EMIs (e.g., Airwallex, Nium, Wise Business) may streamline low-value supplier payments and exotic-currency settlements. Legal constraints: PSD2 licensing/passporting requirements, CSSF notification, MiCA applicability to e-money tokens, and AMLD5 UBO disclosure. Many digital EMIs decline a partnership without legal personality (SCSp), so a BCL-regulated Tier-1 credit institution must remain the clearing, liquidity, and FX anchor.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg market standard requires a physical or bank-approved video KYC interview of the general partner's authorised signatories before onboarding a newly formed SCSp. Remote opening is selectively accepted when UBOs are already banked within the same banking group or when a Luxembourg-regulated fiduciary or management company is engaged. Conservative blueprint: at least one managing partner or authorised director should attend an in-person session in Luxembourg (or at the bank's regional group hub) armed with apostilled identification, certified partnership deed, Luxembourg RCS extract, and original powers of attorney. Post-COVID, BIL and BGL BNP Paribas permit video-verified onboarding for low-risk corporate structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp lacks legal personality — the bank cannot initially evidence the full chain of beneficial ownership from registry filings alone.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO register; deed of partnership identifying the general partner and all limited partners; Luxembourg RCS registration extract; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation for every partner; CRS/FATCA self-certifications; and a signed AML confirmation from the general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-transparent partnership flagged as a potential conduit for treaty shopping or artificial profit shifting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Economic-substance file: registered-office lease contract; local payroll or outsourced administration agreement; board/partner meeting minutes; signed commercial contracts with external suppliers and buyers; invoice-and-settlement trace evidencing arm's-length pricing; and a transfer-pricing memorandum aligned with OECD principles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bulk shipment of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals triggering trade-based money-laundering scrutiny (ambiguous goods description or invoice mismatch).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original commercial invoices; bills of lading or airway bills; phytosanitary certificates; EU-organic or equivalent certification; certificates of origin; independent weight/quality inspection reports (SGS, Intertek, Bureau Veritas); packing lists; underlying supply contracts; and the statutory wholesale licence for herbal botanicals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-screening hits or elevated-risk flags on non-EU buyer or supplier counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-verified screening of each counterparty against EU, UN, OFAC, and UK sanction lists; written compliance certification from counterparties; corporate registry extracts of counterparties; transaction history evidencing legitimate prior dealings; and a written policy on frozen-funds prevention where residual risk remains.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Partner capital is injected via SWIFT MT103 (EUR using SEPA/TARGET2; USD or CNY via correspondent MT103/MT202 COVER) carrying a capital-contribution purpose code (partnership equity). Verification comprises bank credit advice, executed partner resolution, updated capital account entries, and tax-advisor confirmation that the injection is equity rather than debt, preserving the SCSp's pass-through neutrality. Luxembourg applies no exchange controls, so no NOSTRO conversion licence is required; for material contributions, source-of-funds documentation must accompany the transfer so the settling bank can satisfy BCL external statistics and AML obligations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfers with standard trade purpose codes for inventory and supplier settlements; EU suppliers may be settled through SEPA Credit Transfers. For significant consignments, a commercial Letter of Credit (sight L/C) is opened by the SCSp's bank in favour of the supplier, or documentary collections (D/P, D/A) are used. Each disbursement is mirror-matched to the commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, and product certification to satisfy the bank's transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, and AML review.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable FX forward contracts (outright, up to 12 months) executed with a BCL-regulated credit institution under ISDA or a bilateral master agreement.
EUR/USD FX swaps (swap-point, spot-forward) for rolling treasury management and alignment of USD receivables with EUR working-capital requirements.
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for term alignment of long-dated USD trade contracts against EUR cost bases, subject to general-partner authorisation and EMIR reporting as a Non-Financial Counterparty.
Vanilla EUR/USD options (zero-cost collars and put/spread structures) to protect minimum export margins while preserving upside participation.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) restricted to emerging-market supply-chain currencies (e.g., CNY, VND), executed via an EU-authorised counterparty and used solely for cash-flow hedging rather than proprietary speculation.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined aggregate CIT headline rate in Luxembourg City (17% CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax + 7% unemployment-fund surcharge on CIT, i.e., 1.19%); profit tranche up to EUR 200,000 taxed at effective 22.80% combined
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The SCSp is fiscally transparent by statute: no CIT, no net wealth tax, no municipal business tax at partnership level; partners are taxed only upon actual allocation of profits. Luxembourg corporate partners may claim the 100% participation exemption (LIR Art. 147) on qualifying dividend/exit gains; non-resident partners with no Luxembourg PE face 0% Luxembourg taxation on trading income booked outside Luxembourg. No special sectoral incentive for dried goji berry/herbal wholesale (ISIC 4631).
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited - losses may be carried forward indefinitely under LIR Art. 114; carryforward is forfeited where more than 50% of partnership interests change hands and the business activity is not maintained (anti-loss-trading rule).
